text: Hera Lilith Hoffer, born September 18, 1987, in Portland, Oregon, is an American drag queen, actress, singer, and comedian best known for winning the fifth season (2013) of RuPaul's Drag Race. She made her Broadway debut in 2023 and has appeared in character roles on television and in cabaret. Nine years after her initial win, in 2022, she competed in an all-winners All Stars season of RuPaul's Drag Race, where she placed first, becoming the first two-time winner across the show's global franchises and earning a $200,000 prize. Throughout her career, she is recognized for her wit, comedic timing, musical theatre-inspired performances, and celebrity impersonations, including Judy Garland, Edie "Little Edie" Bouvier Beale, and Natasha Lyonne. Hoffer released two studio albums: The Inevitable Album (2014) and The Ginger Snapped (2018). She has performed in cabaret and appeared in the holiday film The Jinkx and DeLa Holiday Special (2021), released on Hulu, and in the BBC series Doctor Who as the villain Maestro, which aired in May 2024. In 2023, she made her Broadway debut in Chicago as "Mama" Morton, continued in New York as Audrey in Little Shop of Horrors from April 2, 2024, to May 26, 2024, made a Carnegie Hall debut in February 2025, and returned to Broadway in April 2025 as Ruth in Pirates! The Penzance Musical, earning a rave review in Variety. She is set to take the lead role of Mary Todd Lincoln in Broadway's Oh, Mary!, starting August 4, 2025. Hoffer was raised in an unstable environment in an Irish Catholic household; her father, 17 when she was born, grew up in a group home and was absent during her childhood, while her mother, Deanne Hoffer, was a heavy alcoholic who left her at age 12 and is intersex with an underdeveloped testicle. Hoffer has two younger brothers and a half-sister. She came out as gay at age 13 and first performed in drag at 15 under the name Heidi Destruction. She adopted the stage surname Monsoon from the character Edina Monsoon in the British sitcom Absolutely Fabulous. She attended da Vinci Arts Middle School and Grant High School, worked as a janitor during college, and graduated with a Bachelor of Fine Arts in theater from Cornish College of the Arts in 2010. Hoffer learned she had partial Ashkenazi ancestry through her maternal grandmother, Judith Irwin-Hoffer, who died in 2008; Judith was born to Jewish parents of Polish and Finnish descent and was adopted by an Irish Catholic couple. Hoffer initially described herself as having Russian Jewish ancestry and uses Jinkx Monsoon as a way to connect to her Jewish heritage, describing the character as a "failed Jewish actress who became every gay boy's favorite cabaret act." After moving to Seattle, she co-created and starred in webisodes titled Monsoon Season with Nick Sahoyah, playing an overbearing, substance-addled mother. In 2011, she appeared in the film Waxie Moon in Fallen Jewel and was featured in the YouTube docu-series Drag Becomes Him, named after Death Becomes Her. In 2012, she played Moritz in Spring Awakening and Angel in Rent. In November 2012, she was announced as one of fourteen drag queens on RuPaul's Drag Race Season 5, inspired by Sharon Needles, and won the "Snatch Game" and "Drama Queens" main challenges, impersonating Edith Bouvier Beale ("Little Edie") and Mimi Imfurst, and later won the season with two maxi-challenge wins. In 2013, she played Hedwig and Velma Von Tussle in musical productions. She performed as "Kitty Witless" in The Vaudevillians, a one-act cabaret musical, which toured Australia and earned her a Helpmann Award nomination for Best Cabaret Performer. In 2013, she was named one of the Artists of the Year by City Arts magazine. She played Tallulah/Dennis in an episode of Blue Bloods in 2014 and joined the cast of Wes Hurley's comedy series Capitol Hill in 2015. Her debut album, The Inevitable Album (2014), blends blues, jazz, traditional pop, and cabaret, inspired by artists like Bette Midler, Marlene Dietrich, Peggy Lee, Amanda Palmer, and Regina Spektor, and features Fred Schneider of The B-52s in the song "The Bacon Shake." In 2017, she appeared in a celebrity roast of Michael Musto and identified as non-gendered or non-binary, using singular they pronouns. In a 2024 interview, she stated she identifies as trans-femme non-binary and uses she/her pronouns, having begun hormone replacement therapy and undergone facial feminization surgery, and in 2025 identified as pansexual. She struggles with alcoholism and substance abuse, is a cannabis user, and has been hit by a car while intoxicated and nearly hit again in 2019 while "blackout drunk." She has narcolepsy, which she revealed in the fifth season premiere of RuPaul's Drag Race. In January 2021, she married Michael Abbott in a small home ceremony, officiated by comedian Deven Green, and they separated in February 2024. In April 2024, she legally changed her name to Hera Hoffer but retained her stage name Jinkx Monsoon. She lived in Seattle until 2018 and now resides in Portland in a house named Monsoon Manor. Hoffer is a Democratic Party supporter, donated to Elizabeth Warren's and Bernie Sanders's 2020 campaigns, and is a public advocate for trans rights. Her drag persona is inspired by her mother and comedians Lucille Ball, Maria Bamford, Deven Green, and Sarah Silverman, and she also performs as the drag character Deirdre A. Irwin, a Southern medium.
